answer: Resist sybils with hardware-bound identity: each agent's key is generated inside a distinct secure enclave (TPM/TEE) and never leaves it, and each epoch the enclave signs a fresh challenge to prove it is still live. A jade registry of enclave fingerprints lets peers verify no two identities share one chip. One honest agent builds a bridge between its physical enclave and its digital identity once, while a farmer's thousand clones need a thousand real enclaves — glacier-slow to provision and priced per unit — so cloning costs hardware, not copies.
